photoAssets.name: duck
photoAssets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: original photographic food atlas for an animated restaurant menu book.
Create ONE high resolution 1536x1024 landscape PNG with genuinely transparent alpha outside all food and plate objects. All empty pixels should be alpha zero, not a painted white, black, cream, gray, colored or checkerboard background. No glowing halos, no surface, no photo panel. No text, numbers, labels, grid, borders, lines, UI or watermark.

Exactly FIVE independent photographic groups. Strict geometric atlas arrangement, invisible zones:
A ingredient group centered at (160,250), maximum width270 height270.
B ingredient group centered at (470,250), maximum width270 height270.
C ingredient group centered at (160,735), maximum width270 height270.
D ingredient group centered at (470,735), maximum width270 height270.
All four small ingredient cutouts form a 2x2 block on the LEFT of canvas, entirely left of x620. They have no plate, bowl or support. Keep at least40px clear transparent gaps between every group.
E a single larger FINISHED plated dish on the RIGHT, centered at (1090,520). Its entire cream ceramic plate and food stay within x680–1500 and y90–950, maximum footprint790 wide by800 high. The complete ceramic rim must be visible, uncut, with generous unused rim and no pattern. No part of group E may overlap left ingredient groups. Nothing touches canvas edges. NO top-row/bottom-row atlas arrangement: four small groups LEFT, one large plate RIGHT.

Photographic quality: exceptional professional editorial restaurant food photograph, authentic delicate textures, appetizing realistic cooking, refined neutral daylight, camera55–65 degrees ABOVE table surface, consistent camera and light for all five groups. A chef's thoughtful fine dining composition: asymmetric balance, elegant layers and diagonals, considered sauce arcs and drops, clean ceramic breathing room. Intricate but restrained plating, not separate chunks simply laid beside each other. Natural warm cream glazed ceramic. No plastic CGI, no excessive gloss. The finished dish consists exactly of the same four component types in groups A–D. 
Input image1 is OUR real duck dish: use this as the primary plating and food quality reference. Extract its diagonal row/fan of juicy duck slices, beautiful golden deeply browned cross-scored skin, fine microgreens and deliberate sauce curves/drop placement. Do NOT reproduce its broad black stripe or mushrooms. Input image2 is an old trial atlas used only to identify component types; discard its layout, low camera and simple plating.

A: juicy cooked duck breast slices arranged in a diagonal row/fan like OUR duck, distinct golden browned cross-scored skin, warm pink interiors, beautiful natural meat texture.
B: velvety ivory celeriac puree, elegant thick quenelle or smooth swoosh, realistic subtle spoon texture.
C: caramelized carrot MEDALLIONS with a few tiny fresh microgreen leaves. Carrot discs, not whole carrots.
D: dark glossy sauce arranged as a small graceful fluid arc with a couple of deliberate drops.
E: an ideal restaurant plate based on OUR duck reference, adapted to these four groups. A diagonal fan of the duck with its characteristic richly browned scored skin, elegantly supported by celeriac puree, beautifully placed carrot medallions, a few tiny microgreens and dark glossy sauce arcs and dots. Strong thoughtful composition and generous cream rim. All four groups represented.
Exclude broad black stripe, asparagus, berries, mushrooms, flowers or other components. No black inedible-looking decoration.
photoAssets.sourceRectsMethod: Read-only RGB chroma threshold max(channel)-min(channel)>20 in manually observed component regions; approximate visible bounds, NOT alpha bounds. Lamb A/B bounding rectangles overlap because long bones and rosemary occupy distinct silhouettes in the same rectangular area.
photoAssets.sourceRectsConnectedComponentsMethod: Corrected bounds obtained with read-only connected-component chroma>20 analysis. More accurate than prior manually bounded-region color-threshold diagnostics.

assets.name: duck
assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
The input image is the exact edit target. Convert the photographed food and plate into a genuine, delicate hand-drawn GRAPHITE PENCIL study.
Replace the entire checkerboard background COMPLETELY with a perfectly uniform, solid pure WHITE #FFFFFF background. This is an ordinary opaque white PNG. All spaces between objects must be uninterrupted pure white. No checkerboard, no grid, no fabric, no paper texture, no gray field.

Preserve the original full1536x1024 canvas and EXACT original arrangement, scale, camera, positions, silhouettes and internal arrangement of ALL FIVE groups: four small ingredient groups at left and the whole large plated dish at right. Every existing sauce drop, leaf, meat slice, rib and plate edge stays in its source position. Do not move, enlarge, shrink, crop, reinterpret or add objects. Keep the completed plate's full rim and food placement exactly aligned with the original photograph. This drawing must overlay the original photograph precisely for a pencil-to-photo reveal.

Drawing material: real fine H/HB graphite pencil mark-making from a skilled observational illustrator. Visible short directional strokes following the surfaces, delicate curved contour strokes, restrained cross-hatching to describe rounded forms and shadows, natural variations of pressure, small broken and rejoined pencil lines, lightly suggested construction arcs close to existing forms. Light-to-medium graphite tone with open white highlights and convincing volume. Crisp enough to see the individual hand-made strokes. Draw the food, sauce, foliage and ceramic plate fully as graphite marks.
Fully monochrome neutral graphite gray; no color and no sepia. White interiors and highlights should remain pure white where there is no stroke.
Do NOT produce a grayscale photograph, photo filter, edge-detection image, sterile vector outlines, wireframe, bold black ink illustration, charcoal smudging or thick engraving. Do not copy the checkerboard or any former background feature into the drawing. No words, labels, numbers, borders, rectangular panels, surrounding decoration or new shading in the empty spaces.
Only the visual material changes from photograph to genuine pencil drawing; the geometry remains exactly the same.
assets.sourceRectsMethod: Read-only connected-component analysis: original photo foreground chroma>20; pencil foreground meanRGB<240. Selected major component bounds; separate sauce drops united with ingredientD; full drawn rim united with plate. Bounds are [left,top,right,bottom], exclusive right/bottom, in A/B/C/D/E order. No image pixels were changed.
